transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-02 16:00 UTC — Duration: 42m — Attendees: Lina (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jamal (Redwood SE), Priya (MicroGrid HO ML), Owen (CTO), Sophie (DevOps), Caleb (legal, joined briefly)

[00:00] Lina: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, i'm lina from redwood, and with me are marcus and jamal on the solutions side.
[00:07] Priya: hey thanks, excited. we run ML infra for microgrids, real-time forecasting, so latency matters.
[00:13] Owen: yes, we have a POC requirement next month and need to decide hosting approach.
[00:20] Marcus: great — high level, redwood gives three paths: hosted api (fastest to first call, PLG credits), dedicated reserved pools for throughput predictability, and private (vpc/onprem) for regulated data. today we can figure out TTFT and security.
[00:36] Sophie: quick question — TTFT meaning how quickly we can go from sign-up to a live infer endpoint?
[00:41] Lina: yep, exactly. with our quickstart credits we typically get dev teams to first token in under an hour, often 15-30 mins if you have your API key and sample prompts ready.
[00:51] Priya: that sounds great. but for production we need KMS integration and audit logs, plus SSO. is that supported in hosted?
[00:59] Jamal: hosted supports SSO and audit logs, but if you require customer-managed KMS and VPC peering, that's where private comes in. dedicated sits in the middle — reserved capacity with stricter isolation but managed keys.
[01:14] Owen: cost is the other axis. we want sub-100ms p99 for small chat-like forecasts but don't want to pay cloud-prohibitive rates. how do you balance batching and latency?
[01:25] Marcus: good question — we expose batching configuration and smart prefix caching. for interactive low-latency use, you can reduce batch windows at the cost of throughput efficiency. our optimize tooling recommends quantization + batch policies given your token distribution; often dedicated with a specific kernel selection gives best cost/latency sweet spot.
[01:44] Sophie: do you have numbers? e.g., gpt-style model latency on A100-ish or commodity gpus?
[01:50] Jamal: our verified profiles show median latencies around 60-120ms for short responses on midsize open models; p99 will vary. we can run a 24hr benchmark with your prompt set to give concrete numbers.
[02:02] Priya: we'd appreciate that. also, are KV cache and prefix caching compatible with private deployment?
[02:07] Marcus: yes, same runtime features across hosted/dedicated/private — that's a core differentiator. occasionally naming in the transcript may be off but features are consistent.
[02:19] Owen: security questions — SOC2 yes? any third-party attestation?
[02:23] Lina: we are SOC2 certified; we also publish an auditor summary. for private deployments we offer optional on-prem packaging and integration with customer KMS/HSM.
[02:33] Caleb (legal): quick clarifying Q — is data at rest encrypted using our KMS when private?
[02:38] Jamal: yes, if you choose private and bring-your-own-kms we can encrypt model cache and logs with your key. hosted uses our managed key by default but we offer SSE-KMS options for enterprise tiers.
[02:49] Sophie: firewall / networking — do you support VPC peering or IP allowlists?
[02:54] Marcus: VPC peering, private endpoints, and dedicated transit options. firewall rules typically are just the egress to our control plane when private; we'll share the exact CIDR list and ports.
[03:06] Priya: ok, so for the POC timeline: we want devs to play with quickstart using credits, then run a 2-week pilot under dedicated or private depending on results. is that feasible?
[03:15] Lina: totally. typical flow: PLG credits for initial integration and validation, then a short reserved pilot. we can provision credits today and get you to a first token in under an hour.
[03:26] Owen: what's the catch — any data residency or retention caveats with hosted credits?
[03:31] Jamal: hosted free credits are for dev data; we retain logs for 30 days for troubleshooting unless you opt into longer retention. for regulated data, private deployment is recommended.
[03:41] Sophie: can the pilot be in our cloud region? we prefer eu-west1.
[03:45] Marcus: yes, we have regions in us-west, eu-west; we can pin traffic. in private we can also run on-prem.
[03:52] Priya: SLA — what availability can we expect on dedicated?
[03:56] Lina: enterprise dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA doc in the packet.
[04:03] Owen: let's talk observability — how do we trace request-level costs and latency?
[04:08] Jamal: console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks you can pipe into your APM. plus rollouts and canaries for model versions.
[04:21] Sophie: any red flags on our side? we have strict egress controls and internal KMS that must remain the source of truth.
[04:28] Marcus: that's ok; private with customer-managed KMS is the right fit for production. for pilot you can use hosted while we prep the private connectivity.
[04:38] Priya: can you give an example pricing scenario — 50k tokens/day at 1M tokens/month?
[04:44] Lina: ballpark, hosted per-token rates are lower for open models; dedicated reservation pricing reduces unit costs as you commit. i'll send a few sample spreadsheets based on your token profile.
[04:55] Owen: we'd like to compare OtherCloud AI and LatentOps; what are your differences?
[04:59] Lina: compared to OtherCloud AI we emphasize production throughput and predictable unit economics; compared to LatentOps we provide a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private so you don't rewrite for private. but we'll include a competitive note.
[05:14] Sophie: can you provision credits and share the quickstart link now? we'd like to try an internal spike.
[05:19] Lina: yes — i'll provision a 90-day dev credit bundle and email the setup link + sample prompts.
[05:26] Marcus: for the technical deep dive, we'll scope a 60-90 minute session to go through VPC peering, firewall rules, and a latency benchmarking plan.
[05:34] Priya: sounds good, we'll gather the prompt set and success metrics (p50/p95 latency, token cost per request, accuracy metrics) and send to marcus.
[05:43] Owen: legal will want a quick look at data retention and encryption details. caleb will follow up.
[05:49] Caleb: yep will do.
[05:51] Lina: recap: lina sends pricing + credits + SOC2 and deployment docs; marcus sends network diagram and benchmark plan; priya sends prompt set and criteria; sophie confirms firewall/kms needs. any other items?
[06:05] Priya: no, that's it. thanks.
[06:08] Lina: great, talk soon. bye.

End transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional name mismatches and imperfect punctuation; timestamps approximate and inserted every ~15-60s.
